questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “MCU, memory, and pins”?
options: Compile and upload are separate; a successful build does not guarantee the selected port is correct.
Record the board package version so the build can be reproduced.
Peripheral and pin mappings depend on the board's MCU.
questions.answer: Peripheral and pin mappings depend on the board's MCU.
questions.explanation:
Peripheral and pin mappings depend on the board's MCU.
Why: A microcontroller combines a CPU, memory, and I/O peripherals. RAM is working memory, flash stores firmware, and pin capabilities depend on the board's datasheet.

Origin and date: the Arduino project began in 2005 in Ivrea, Italy, for education and physical computing. Arduino's official About page names Massimo Banzi, David Cuartielles, Tom Igoe, and David Mellis as co-founders. Its purpose was to lower the barrier between electronics and programming by making sensor-and-actuator projects approachable with an affordable board. Arduino is used in prototypes, education, measurement instruments, and IoT devices; it connects to careers in embedded development, electronics prototyping, and test engineering. If building systems that sense and affect the physical world inspires you, start by learning how pins, RAM, and flash fit together.
